title: Check yourself: Service levels, feedback and the lifecycle from pilot to scale

questions.stem: Scenario: Ola's team reports its latency service level, a ceiling of 2000 ms at the 95th percentile. The week's measured figure is exactly 2000 ms. How does the report read?

options.text: Missed by 0 ms, since the measure has reached the limit
options.says: Ruled out because "A latency of 2000 ms against a ceiling of 2000 ms is met".

options.text: Met, since a value at the limit counts as inside it
options.says: A service level is met at its limit exactly.

options.text: Met, but with the ceiling raised to 2100 ms for the week
options.says: Ruled out because the ceiling is the target, and "Met at the limit exactly" leaves no reason to raise it.

options.text: Undecided until a second week of measurements arrives
options.says: Ruled out because "Met at the limit exactly" settles the case without a second week.

origin.section: A service level has three parts

questions.stem: Scenario: Vera is writing the pilot table for a billing assistant and offers the stop trigger "if the quality is worse than we hoped". What is wrong with it?

options.text: It should name the reviewer who decides when quality is poor enough
options.says: Ruled out because a trigger worded as "if it goes wrong" "is not a trigger", whoever decides.

options.text: It states a quality aim, which belongs to the sponsor and not the pilot
options.says: Ruled out because "the stop trigger is the pilot's own", so the aim may be the sponsor's while the trigger is not.

options.text: It should come after the roll-out so that the data exists to judge it
options.says: Ruled out because the record lists each assumption "with a test and a stop trigger that has a number in it" before the pilot runs.

options.text: It holds no number, so reaching it is a matter of opinion
options.says: A trigger needs a number to be reached.
